nodes.title: Procfile
nodes.summary: Heroku process definition file specifying two process types: a release phase that runs Prisma migrations against the API schema, and a web process that boots the compiled Node.js API server.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Heroku Procfile syntax — a declarative key:value format (not a programming language). Each line maps a process type to a shell command.
nodes.languageLesson: Procfile is a Heroku-specific declarative format: each line is `process_type: command`. The `release` type runs once before each deploy; `web` binds to $PORT for incoming HTTP traffic.

relationships.note: release phase runs Prisma migrate deploy against this schema
web process boots the compiled API entry point
both configure Heroku deployment; Procfile defines runtime processes while package.json defines the heroku-postbuild hook

nodes.title: opencode-session.json
nodes.summary: Auto-generated OpenCode AI assistant session log capturing the full conversation history, tool invocations, model metadata (gemini-2.5-flash), token usage statistics, and cost accounting for a planning session. Not application source code.
nodes.languageNotes: JSON. This is a machine-generated session transcript from the OpenCode CLI tool, not hand-written application code. It contains structured conversation turns with tool results and metadata.
nodes.languageLesson: OpenCode session files store full conversation state as JSON arrays of message objects. They include token counts, cost estimates, and tool call results for replay/audit purposes.

relationships.note: written by the OpenCode coding assistant tool during development sessions

nodes.title: package.json
nodes.summary: Root monorepo manifest for pavati-pustak. Defines npm workspaces (packages/*, apps/*), orchestrates build/test/typecheck across all workspaces, configures Heroku postbuild (Prisma generate + build), and declares shared devDependencies (concurrently, TypeScript 5.6).
nodes.languageNotes: Standard npm package.json with monorepo workspace fields. The `workspaces` array and workspace-prefixed scripts (`npm run X -w @pavati/Y`) are npm's native monorepo support.
nodes.languageLesson: npm workspaces use a root package.json with a `workspaces` glob array. Scripts reference sub-packages via `-w @scope/name`. The `heroku-postbuild` script is a Heroku lifecycle hook that runs after `npm install`.

relationships.note: workspaces glob includes all packages under apps/
workspaces glob includes all packages under packages/
heroku-postbuild runs prisma generate against the API schema
both are root config; package.json governs dependencies and scripts while tsconfig governs compilation
both configure Heroku deployment — package.json defines postbuild, Procfile defines runtime processes

nodes.title: tsconfig.base.json
nodes.summary: Shared base TypeScript configuration inherited by all workspace packages. Targets ES2022 with ESNext modules and Bundler resolution, enables strict mode with additional checks (noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters, noFallthroughCasesInSwitch), and supports both Node and DOM lib environments.
nodes.languageNotes: TypeScript compiler options in JSON. This is a base config (no `files`/`include`) designed to be extended via `extends` in each workspace's tsconfig.json. The Bundler moduleResolution is optimized for modern bundlers (Vite, esbuild).
nodes.languageLesson: A tsconfig.base.json pattern separates compiler options (shared) from file inclusion (per-package). Child configs extend it with `{ "extends": "../../tsconfig.base.json" }` and add their own `include`/`exclude`.

relationships.note: each workspace package extends this base config
each shared package extends this base config
complementary root configs — tsconfig for compilation, package.json for dependencies/scripts
